column15: How does this relate to rail/rail_crossing edge? Yep, they conflict. rail_crossing attribute on edges says to use virtual nodes to connect a crossing (with rail_crossing = "yes") to sidewalk/other edges. I think the rail_crossing node got split out to capture details that might be different on different sides of the crossing (ex. there are tactile markings approaching from the east but not from the west). Maybe the best reconciliation is to keep this and the rail_crossing edge and drop the use of virtual nodes/edges, so we keep all the details people want. In that case, it might make more sense to have it be a node type rather than a node attribute. - Jay
